content: Obesity is a medical condition characterized by an excessive accumulation of fat in the body, particularly in the subcutaneous connective tissue, which serves as the natural energy reserve in humans and other mammals. This excessive fat storage reaches a level where it is associated with an increased risk of various health conditions and higher mortality rates. While obesity is considered an individual clinical condition, it is increasingly recognized as a significant and growing public health issue. Excessive body weight has been shown to predispose individuals to a range of diseases, including cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes mellitus, sleep apnea, and osteoarthritis. A higher BMI is strongly associated with an elevated risk of developing potentially life-threatening medical complications. Obesity is not merely a cosmetic concern but a complex medical disorder with significant implications for overall health and quality of life.
